column1: # LERENA AND LLERENA, ALTERNATING FOR ONE MAN - the test hypothesis 1 asked for.
# Sources attached to Sancho Llerena Aguilar (FamilySearch Tree LHJP-D1Y, b. Cordoba 1767,
# d. 1832, m. Canelones 1791), every one of them in "Uruguay, registros parroquiales, 1726-2000".
# Listed exactly as the source titles render his name. Read 13 September 2026.
# *** TIER: the ATTACHMENTS are secondary - a tree user decided these fourteen records are all
# the same man, and the underlying acts have NOT been opened here. What is primary and checkable
# is that the Uruguayan parish registers of one city spell this name BOTH WAYS across forty years.

# NOTE the 1828 form: "Sancho DE Llerena" - the toponymic construction, "of Llerena", which is
# how the Badajoz town-name behaves as a surname. It is the strongest single form in the list.
# ================ *** A FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP, FOUND 14 September 2026 *** ================
# A full-text search for the exact phrase "SANCHO LLERENA" returns FOUR PAGES of results. Page one is
# this family, in Uruguay. *** PAGES TWO TO FOUR ARE ALMOST ENTIRELY SPANISH NOBILITY PROOFS, NOTARIAL
# BOOKS AND MILITARY RECORDS - and not one of them contains a man called Sancho Llerena. ***
# One was opened to check: Alcantara, Caceres, Extremadura, Military Records 1599, ark
# 3:1:3Q9M-CSLC-7CX8 - a proof of nobility for the Order of Alcantara. The transcript reads:
#     "...sin tener mesada, ni taca alguna de judios, moros, ni herejes, ni penitenciados por el
#      *** SANCHO , OFICIO *** ... es familiar del *** SANCHO , OFICIO LLERENA ***"
# *** IT IS "SANTO OFICIO ... LLERENA" - THE INQUISITION TRIBUNAL SEATED AT LLERENA, BADAJOZ. *** The
# man is a FAMILIAR DEL SANTO OFICIO de Llerena. The machine reads "Santo Oficio" as "Sancho, oficio"
# and the phrase search then matches "Sancho ... Llerena" across the two words.
# *** WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO WRITE DOWN. *** The Inquisition had a tribunal at Llerena for three
# centuries, so the words "Santo Oficio" and "Llerena" sit next to each other in THOUSANDS of Spanish
# documents. *** Any search for this family in Spain will drown in them, *** and this archive was one
# step from recording "Sancho is an attested forename in Spanish Llerena families" - which would have
# been false, and would have been quietly used to argue against FRANCISCO.
# *** THE SPANISH ORIGIN QUESTION IS THEREFORE UNTOUCHED BY ANY OF THIS. *** The census still says
# "Andaluzia"; CORDOBA still comes only from a tree; and the surname's home town of Llerena is in
# EXTREMADURA, not Andalusia - which is a real tension this archive has not resolved and must not
# pretend it has. See the "Basque or Extremaduran?" question on /open-questions/.
